readerTitle: Your profit doubled. How much of it actually happened this year?
caseNote: 가상 시뮬레이션 (가전 매장 + 설치·점검 서비스) · 모든 수치는 설명용
insight: 이익이 늘었을 때는 '얼마나'보다 '언제 번 돈인가'를 먼저 묻는다. 시점과 분류만 바꿔도 좋은 해처럼 보일 수 있다.
misconception: 통장에 돈이 들어왔거나 청구서를 보냈으면 올해 이익이다. 오래 가는 지출은 모두 자산으로 잡아도 된다.

sources.text: 재무회계의 표준 개념 (발생주의, 수익 인식, 선수수익, 자본적 지출과 수익적 지출 구분, 이익의 질)

factChecks.note: 서비스 플랜: 가을 판매, 올해 제공분 약 $4,000은 가정입니다. 균등 분할(연 $12,000)이 아니라 제공한 서비스만큼 인식한다는 설명이 일반 원칙에 맞는지 검토하세요.
도장·소모 부품 교체를 비용으로 본 것은 '기존 상태 유지'라는 일반 원칙에 따른 단순화입니다. 실제 분류와 세무 처리는 나라와 금액 기준에 따라 다르므로 카드에 회계사 확인을 권했습니다.
softwareNote: $1,200 연간 구독을 12월에 계약하면 올해 수익 $100(1개월분)으로 계산했습니다. 12월 1일 시작 가정.

cards.title: Your appliance store's profit more than doubled.
body: You sell washers, fridges and ovens, and your team installs and services them. Last year the business made $40,000 in profit. This year the bookkeeper's draft says **$90,000**.
Next week you meet the bank about a loan for a second store. Before you go, you check where the extra $50,000 came from.

image.label: Store owner reading a year-end report in an appliance showroom
image.brief: 가전 매장 쇼룸, 세탁기와 냉장고 사이에서 사장이 연말 보고서를 들고 있음. 보고서에 "$90,000"이 크게 보이고, 그 옆에 작은 돋보기. 실제 브랜드 로고는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: $36,000 of three-year service plans
body: This autumn you ran a promotion: pay once, get three years of maintenance visits. Customers paid $36,000. The bookkeeper counted all of it as this year's revenue. Only about $4,000 of visits have happened so far.
How should this year's books show it?

options.text: Keep all $36,000. The cash is in the bank
options.feedback: Profit looks great now, but you still owe about $32,000 of visits. The next two years carry the cost of that work with none of the revenue.

options.text: Count $4,000 now and record $32,000 as owed to customers until the visits happen
options.feedback: Profit drops by $32,000 this year, but each year now matches the work done. The cash stays. It just isn't profit yet.

options.text: Split it evenly: $12,000 a year for three years
options.feedback: Closer, but revenue should follow the work delivered. Most plans started in autumn, so only about $4,000 is earned this year.

cards.title: Say you spread the plans. Next: a December invoice.
body: A builder ordered 30 appliances for new apartments. You invoiced $30,000 in December. The appliances sit in your warehouse until delivery in March. They cost you $21,000.
Does this sale belong in this year?

options.text: Yes. The invoice is sent and the builder agreed to pay
options.feedback: Sending a bill doesn't finish the job. If the project slips or the order changes, this year's profit was never real.

options.text: No. Count it in March, when it's delivered. Until then the appliances stay as stock
options.feedback: This year's profit falls by $9,000, the $30,000 sale minus its $21,000 cost. Next year gets a sale that's actually done.

options.text: Count it now only if the builder paid a deposit
options.feedback: A deposit helps your cash, but it's money received before the work. It's owed to the builder until delivery.

cards.title: Say you moved the order to March. Last: the paint job.
body: You spent $12,000 repainting the showroom and replacing worn fittings. The bookkeeper recorded it as an asset called "store improvements", to spread over five years.

options.text: Keep it as an asset. The paint will last for years
options.feedback: Most repairs last a while. Treating upkeep as an asset pushes normal running costs into later years and flatters today.

options.text: Count it as this year's expense. It keeps the store as it was rather than adding something new
options.feedback: Profit falls by $12,000, but honestly: this is the regular cost of running a showroom.

options.text: Keep it as an asset, but spread it over two years
options.feedback: Less distortion, but still the wrong label. A shorter spread only hides less of the cost.

cards.title: From $90,000 to $37,000.
cards.callout: The jump came from timing and labels, not a better year.
cards.softwareNote: Annual plans paid upfront work the same way. A $1,200 yearly subscription that starts on December 1 adds $100 of revenue this year, not $1,200. The rest is service you still owe.

cards.title: Quality of earnings
body: **Quality of earnings** asks how much of a reported profit comes from work actually done this year, matched with its true costs, in a way that can repeat.
No one made an arithmetic mistake here. Each item simply landed in the wrong year: revenue counted early, a cost counted late.
The good news: the $32,000 of plans and the March sale aren't lost. They become profit when you earn them.

image.label: Profit blocks being moved from this year into next years
image.brief: 달력 세 칸(This year, Next year, Year after). 'This year' 칸에 쌓여 있던 블록 일부를 손이 다음 해 칸으로 옮기는 장면. 블록 라벨: "Service plans", "Builder order".

cards.title: Don't swing to the lowest number.
body: Cleaning up profit doesn't mean making it as small as possible. Expensing a new delivery van in one year would distort the picture the other way.

Some calls are genuinely grey. Is new flooring a repair or an upgrade? Write down the rule you used and apply it every year. Tax rules can differ from these, so check with an accountant in your country.

cards.title: Say you expensed the repairs. Now, the bank.
body: The loan officer asks for this year's profit. You have the draft $90,000 and the cleaned-up $37,000. What do you bring?

options.text: The $90,000 draft. It's what the books said
options.feedback: It might win the meeting. When the bank's own review finds the timing issues, your credibility goes with it.

options.text: The $37,000, with a note on the $32,000 of plans and the March order coming next year
options.feedback: A smaller number, but one a lender can trust. It also shows revenue already lined up.

options.text: Both numbers, and let the bank decide which counts
options.feedback: Open, but it hands the judgment to someone else. The bank wants to know which number you believe.

cards.title: Profit is real when it's earned, matched and repeatable.
body: Each decision used one idea from this unit:
list: **Service plans:** money received before it's earned
cards.callout: **Try it today:** find the biggest single item in last year's profit. Ask two things: was the work done, and does its cost sit in the same year?
